verses.text: The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and tell them: A priest must not make himself unclean by touching a dead body among his people,
except for a close relative: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
or an unmarried sister who depends on him because she has no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.
He must not make himself unclean for people related to him by marriage, and so make himself unfit for holy work.
Priests must not shave their heads, or shave the edges of their beards, or cut their bodies.
They must be holy to their God and not dishonour his name. They offer the gifts made by fire to the LORD, the food of their God, so they must be holy.
A priest must not marry a woman who has been a prostitute or who is not pure, or a woman divorced from her husband, because the priest is holy to his God.
Treat him as holy, because he offers the food of your God. He must be holy to you, because I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy.
If a priest's daughter dishonours herself by becoming a prostitute, she dishonours her father. She must be burned in the fire.

The high priest, the one among his brothers who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been set apart to wear the priestly clothes, must not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes to mourn.
He must not go near any dead body. He must not make himself unclean, even for his father or mother.
He must not leave the holy place to mourn, or he will dishonour the holy place of his God, because the anointing oil of his God is on him like a crown. I am the LORD.
The woman he marries must be a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who is not pure, or a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not dishonour his children among his people. I am the LORD, who makes him holy."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron: For all time to come, none of your descendants who has something wrong with his body may come near to offer the food of his God.
No man who has something wrong with his body may come near: no one who is blind or lame, or who has a damaged face or a deformed body,
no one with a crippled foot or hand,
no one who has a hunched back or is very small, no one with an eye problem, an itching skin disease, or sores, and no one whose private parts are damaged.

No descendant of Aaron the priest who has something wrong with his body may come near to offer the gifts made by fire to the LORD. Since he has something wrong with him, he must not come near to offer the food of his God.
He may still eat the food of his God, both the most holy food and the holy food.
But he must not go near the curtain or come near the altar, because he has something wrong with his body. He must not dishonour my holy places, for I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
So Moses told this to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel.
